assessment.overall_rationale: Both settings decompose the cilia biology into a broad structural-assembly module (L1≈R1, strong same_core match) and a narrower functional/signaling module, but the right setting's second cilia module (R2) centers on BBSome-Hedgehog GPCR trafficking whereas the left's second module (L2) centers on endothelial mechanosensation of blood flow, giving only partial overlap across that pairing in both directions; the left's third module is a Wnt/Fzd4-Gata2-Eng BBB angiogenesis program while the right's third module is an unrelated mitochondrial proteostasis cluster, so these have essentially no correspondence except a shared Fzd4 regulator touching R1 and weak tissue-context ties to R3.

pair_scores.rationale: Both describe the same core cilia biogenesis mechanism (IFT-B, transition zone, distal appendage machinery) using almost identical gene sets, differing only in which BBSome/CPLANE gene is emphasized.
Shares Bbs9/Nme7/Tbc1d32 and the cilia domain, but R2's core mechanism is Hedgehog-GPCR signaling output while L1's is structural ciliary assembly/trafficking.
Cilia biogenesis machinery has no mechanistic or gene overlap with mitochondrial inner membrane/protein maturation biology.
Same cilia gene set and tissue context, but L2's central claim is endothelial shear-stress mechanotransduction whereas R1's core mechanism is structural ciliogenesis assembly.
Both concern functional/signaling output of cilia rather than pure assembly, but L2's mechanism is flow-induced mechanosensation (KLF2/MAPK) versus R2's Hedgehog-GPCR trafficking output.
Only a peripheral tissue link (brain barrier-forming endothelium metabolic demand) connects endothelial cilia mechanosensing to mitochondrial proteostasis; mechanisms are unrelated.
Shares the Fzd4 regulator, but L3's core mechanism is Norrin/Wnt-BBB signaling while R1's core mechanism is ciliary structural assembly, so overlap is regulator-only, not mechanistic.
Wnt-Fzd4/Gata2/Eng-driven BBB angiogenic identity shares no genes, regulators, or mechanism with BBSome-Hedgehog ciliary GPCR trafficking.

Only a loose contextual link exists (mitochondrial support for barrier-forming endothelium) between BBB angiogenic signaling and mitochondrial cristae/protein biogenesis, with no shared genes or mechanism.
